newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end stronger on high volume.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end stronger on high volume.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Wednesday in the heaviest volume in three years in response to a cut in the Bank of Israel's key lending rate, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.20 percent, or 3.51 points, to 296.81 on all-share turnover of 308 million shekels against 220 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.15 percent higher at 305.83.
Before the end of the session, the central bank announced it would cut its main lending rate by 1.2 percentage points to an annual 12.7 percent. It was the first rate reduction since February.

"The market is rising as a result of the interest rate cut. The alternative to stocks -- bonds -- will become less attractive because of lower yields. The market has gotten a push because of this," said Ilan Doron of Sold Financial Markets.
Doron said the cabinet's decision to reform the foreign exchange regime was positive because it would make the market more free and the shekel more convertible.
"(Finance Minister Dan) Meridor's resignation did not affect the market at all. There are some fears about who will replace him but today the market is only reacting to positive news," Doron said.
Meridor quit early on Wednesday after the cabinet decided against his advice to widen the shekel's trading bands.
"The market is rising because they made a good economic deal with a very nice cut in interest rates, which lowers financing costs for companies," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments.
"Only a week ago we dreamt of a 0.5 percentage point cut. We were afraid of an appreciation (of the shekel) but didn't get one. At the moment the dollar is rising," Halpern said.
Traders said foreign investors were very active on the buying side on Wednesday.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which climbed 2.0 percent to 573 agorot on turnover of 24.6 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 2.0 percent to 32,831 agorot on volume of 16.1 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which fell 0.75 percent to 801 agorot on volume of 16 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
